a Dutch family displayed a 1.8 kb genomic deletion that removes exon 9 and results in the absence of seven amino acids in a conserved SEA domain of the IMPG2 protein

records.label: Additional index cases with IMPG2 nonsense mutations
quotes: Mutation analysis in ten additional index cases that were of Dutch, Israeli, Italian, and Pakistani origin and had homozygous regions encompassing IMPG2 revealed five additional mutations; four nonsense mutations and one missense mutation affecting a highly conserved phenylalanine residue.
Most patients with IMPG2 mutations showed an early-onset form of RP with progressive visual-field loss and deterioration of visual acuity.

notes.statement: Meunier et al. (2014) screened 49 families with vitelliform macular dystrophy who had no BEST1 or PRPH2 mutation. In 1 family, 2 patients with autosomal dominant adult-onset vitelliform dystrophy carried a heterozygous c.3230G-T (p.Cys1077Phe) mutation in IMPG2. This is an allelic macular phenotype rather than retinitis pigmentosa.
quotes: IMPG1 was the causal gene in 3 families (IMPG1 1-3, 11 patients) and IMPG2 in a fourth family (2 patients).
With an autosomal dominant transmission, families 1 and 2 had the c.713T→G (p.Leu238Arg) mutation in IMPG1 and family 4 had the c.3230G→T (p.Cys1077Phe) mutation in IMPG2.

notes.statement: Bandah-Rozenfeld et al. (2010) used autozygosity mapping to identify 2 families, each with 3 affected sibs, sharing large overlapping homozygous regions on chromosome 3 that contained the IMPG2 gene.
quotes: Using autozygosity mapping, we identified two families, each with three affected siblings sharing large overlapping homozygous regions that harbored the IMPG2 gene on chromosome 3.

notes.statement: Bandah-Rozenfeld et al. (2010) found that in transiently transfected COS-1 cells, a construct expressing the wildtype IMPG2 SEA domain was targeted to the plasma membrane, whereas the mutant lacking 7 amino acids (from the exon 9 deletion) appeared to be retained in the endoplasmic reticulum.
quotes: Transient transfection of COS-1 cells showed that a construct expressing the wild-type SEA domain is properly targeted to the plasma membrane, whereas the mutant lacking the seven amino acids appears to be retained in the endoplasmic reticulum.

notes.statement: Bandah-Rozenfeld et al. (2010) reported that most patients with IMPG2 mutations had early-onset RP with progressive visual field loss and declining visual acuity, whereas the patient with a missense mutation was diagnosed with maculopathy.
quotes: Most patients with IMPG2 mutations showed an early-onset form of RP with progressive visual-field loss and deterioration of visual acuity. The patient with the missense mutation, however, was diagnosed with maculopathy.
